title: Retention policy evaluation engine: precedence, effective policy computation, caching, determinism tests
creator: Jordan Lee
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — Retention Controls v1
description:
Context
We’re implementing tenant-configurable retention controls across audit logs + select operational/telemetry datasets. ENG-2911 adds schema + validation and persists retention policies. This ticket updates the policy evaluation engine (library + service surfaces) that computes an “effective policy” for a given tenant/env/region/dataType and is used by:
- retention enforcement workers (e.g., audit logs worker, eligible telemetry TTL)
- Console “Effective policy” view and enforcement status panels
- compliance reporting pack evidence snapshots (policy attestations)

We must guarantee:
- correct precedence rules (org/tenant/env) and deterministic results across services
- guardrails are enforced (min/max retention, disallow “never delete” unless explicitly permitted)
- legal hold and exceptions override deletion while preserving auditability
- caching does not lead to stale or inconsistent enforcement

Goals
1) Precedence rules and effective-policy computation are defined, implemented, and covered by golden tests.
2) Add caching for evaluation to avoid repeated DB reads / JSON parsing on hot paths.
3) Determinism tests: ensure evaluation is stable regardless of input ordering, JSON formatting, or map iteration ordering.
4) Provide a clear contract for “why” a value was chosen (provenance) to support Console transparency and audit evidence.

Non-goals (v1)
- full retention customization for every internal log stream (some governed by SRE/vendor constraints)
- customer-configurable retention for raw inference payload contents
- generalized policy language beyond retention (keep scope limited to retention policy model)

Design / Decisions
A) Inputs / policy layers
We support these layers (highest precedence wins):
1. Tenant override policy (tenant_id)
2. Org default policy (org_id) — only applicable for multi-tenant orgs; for single-tenant accounts, org == tenant but we keep the concept for future-proofing
3. System defaults (hardcoded by product tier / deployment mode)

Within a policy document, allow per-environment overrides:
- environments: production | staging | development (strings, validated)
- for Private deployments, allow “deployment_id” scoping in the future but not in v1

Within an environment, allow optional per-region override:
- region key names match control plane region IDs (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1)

Within each (env, region), allow per-dataType entries:
- audit_logs
- admin_activity
- inference_request_metadata (metadata only; see product scope)
- telemetry_analytics (eligible tables only)
- operational_logs (where applicable; may be marked “not configurable” per deployment)

B) Precedence rule for selecting a retention value
Effective retention for a given (tenant, env, region, dataType) is selected by the following resolution order:
1. Tenant policy: env+region+dataType exact match
2. Tenant policy: env+dataType match (no region)
3. Tenant policy: global+dataType match (no env, no region)
4. Org policy: env+region+dataType exact match
5. Org policy: env+dataType match
6. Org policy: global+dataType match
7. System default for (deployment_mode, tier, dataType)

If a dataType is not configurable for a deployment mode (e.g., certain infra operational logs), evaluation returns:
- effective_retention_days = system default
- configurable = false
- notes include why (e.g., “governed by SRE baseline; vendor retention fixed at X days”)

C) Guardrails and normalization
- Retention is expressed in whole days (integer). We normalize any input to integer days at validation time (ENG-2911), but evaluation also treats invalid/missing values defensively.
- Apply min/max guardrails at evaluation time as a second line of defense (in case of old tenants / migrated rows). Guardrail source: system config (per dataType/per deployment mode).
- “never delete” is represented as retention_days = 0 only for internal/system datasets; for customer-configurable datasets we treat 0 as invalid and fall back to default + emit an evaluation warning.

D) Legal hold / exception semantics
Legal hold is not a “retention days” concept; it’s an enforcement override. Evaluation returns both:
- effective_retention_days (what the policy says)
- enforcement_state (normal | legal_hold | exception)

When legal_hold=true:
- enforcement workers must NOT delete records for affected datasets within scope
- Console must display a banner “Legal hold active” and show who/when initiated (ENG-2934 for data model)
- Compliance evidence should still show the underlying retention policy and clearly indicate hold is overriding deletion

E) Provenance / explainability
Return a provenance object (as serialized string for now) including:
- chosen_layer: tenant|org|system
- matched_scope: global|env|env+region
- policy_version_id (if persisted)
- matched_rule_path (e.g., tenant.production.us-east-1.audit_logs)

Note: we will keep the core evaluation library returning a struct internally; APIs can serialize provenance into a stable JSON string for Console and evidence snapshots.

Implementation Plan
1) Evaluation library
- Create/extend retention-policy-eval package used by control plane and workers.
- Primary function:
  evaluateRetention(tenantId, orgId, env, region, dataType, deploymentMode, tier, now)
  -> returns effective_retention_days, enforcement_state, configurable, provenance_json, warnings
- Provide helper to compute “effective policy summary” for Console:
  computeEffectivePolicy(tenantId, env, region)
  -> list of dataTypes with resolved values + provenance

2) Caching
- Add an in-process cache keyed by (tenantId, orgId, env, region, deploymentMode, tier, policy_updated_at)
- Cache value: pre-parsed policy documents + resolved summary for a given env/region
- TTL: 60s (configurable); max size: 10k entries per instance
- Invalidation:
  - incorporate policy_updated_at from DB row (ENG-2911 schema) into cache key so updates naturally miss cache
  - ensure “policy_updated_at” is monotonically increasing (DB trigger or app-set)
- For enforcement workers: keep a short TTL to reduce DB load but avoid long-lived staleness; workers re-fetch effective policy at the start of each batch window.

3) Determinism / golden tests
- Add golden test vectors covering:
  - precedence (tenant overrides org; env overrides global; region overrides env)
  - missing keys and partial documents
  - invalid 0 retention for customer-configurable dataTypes
  - guardrail clamping behavior
  - non-configurable dataset returning system defaults + configurable=false
  - legal hold state overrides enforcement_state but does not change effective_retention_days
- Determinism properties:
  - JSON field order changes do not change effective output
  - map iteration order does not affect selection
  - whitespace differences do not change output
  - provenance_json is stable (sorted keys) to avoid noisy diffs in evidence snapshots

4) Observability hooks
- Add a counter for policy evaluation calls and cache hit rate (tagged by service and dataType)
- Add a warning log (rate-limited) when evaluation clamps values due to guardrails or sees invalid values

Acceptance Criteria
- Effective policy computation matches documented precedence rules; tests cover all resolution branches.
- Determinism: running evaluation across randomized JSON key ordering yields identical outputs and stable provenance_json.
- Cache hit rate >80% on Console effective-policy endpoint under typical UI usage (measured in staging).
- No regression in enforcement workers: they can compute effective policy without additional DB round-trips per record (per batch only).
- Security sign-off: no path allows “never delete” for customer-configurable datasets without explicit system permission.

Risk / Notes
- Staleness risk: caching must be keyed on policy_updated_at; do not rely purely on TTL.
- Provenance stability matters for compliance pack evidence snapshots; ensure canonical JSON serialization.
- Ensure evaluation library is used consistently across control plane, Console backend, and workers to avoid divergent behavior.

Links
- ENG-2911 (schema + validation): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2911
- ENG-2934 (legal hold + exceptions): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2934
- PM initiative ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-482
- Related PR (expected): sources/github/redwood/pr-18437.json (effective-policy computation + golden tests)

Rollout
- Feature-flag gated: retentionPolicyEvaluationV2
- Stage 1 (staging): enable for internal tenants, compare outputs vs v1 evaluation in shadow mode (log diff only)
- Stage 2 (hosted canary): enable for small set of enterprise tenants (Naomi to provide list)
- Stage 3: make V2 default; keep v1 fallback for 2 weeks, then delete
